meta.description: Presents and manages the main navigation menu for regular (non-admin) users of the CardDemo credit card management system, allowing them to select and launch available functional modules.
meta.process_description: Upon entry, the program validates that a user session exists (communication area is populated); if not, it redirects the user back to the sign-on screen. For authenticated regular users, it dynamically builds and displays a numbered menu of up to 12 available options sourced from the shared communication area, showing the current date and time in the screen header. When the user selects an option by entering a number and pressing Enter, the program validates the selection, enforces access control (blocking admin-only options from regular users), and transfers control to the corresponding functional program via CICS XCTL. Pressing PF3 returns the user to the sign-on screen, and any unsupported key press results in an error message being displayed on the menu screen.

files.USRSEC: User security file used to validate user credentials and role/type during session management

business_rules: A valid authenticated session (non-zero communication area) must exist before the menu is displayed; otherwise the user is redirected to the sign-on screen.
Regular users are explicitly blocked from selecting menu options designated as 'Admin Only' (CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE = 'A'); an access-denied message is displayed if attempted.
Only numeric option values within the valid range (1 to CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT) are accepted; non-numeric, zero, or out-of-range entries result in a validation error message.

Menu options mapped to programs with a name beginning with 'DUMMY' are treated as placeholder features not yet implemented, and the user is informed they are 'coming soon' without any program transfer occurring.

Menu options mapped to the program 'COPAUS0C' are subject to an additional runtime availability check (CICS INQUIRE); if the program is not installed, the user is informed rather than an error being thrown.
Pressing PF3 at any time returns the user to the sign-on screen (COSGN00C), effectively ending the current session navigation.
Any key press other than Enter or PF3 is treated as invalid and results in an error message being displayed on the menu screen without any navigation occurring.
The menu supports a maximum of 12 displayable options; any options beyond 12 in the communication area are silently ignored.

variables.name: WS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Group record containing all working storage variables used during menu session processing for the CardDemo main user menu screen.

variables.name: WS-PGMNAME
variables.description: The internal CICS program name of this menu program (COMEN01C). Used to identify the currently executing program when passing control between screens or logging navigation context within the CardDemo session.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction identifier (CM00) associated with the main user menu. Used to re-invoke this menu screen when the user returns from a sub-function, ensuring the session stays anchored to the correct transaction context.

variables.name: WS-MESSAGE
variables.description: The user-facing feedback message displayed at the bottom of the menu screen. Contains validation errors (e.g., invalid option selected, access denied for admin-only options, feature not yet available) or informational notices to guide the user's next action.

variables.name: WS-USRSEC-FILE
variables.description: The name of the User Security file (USRSEC) used to validate user credentials and determine user role (regular user vs. admin) during session management. Referenced when performing access control checks before displaying or navigating the menu.

variables.name: WS-ERR-FLG
variables.description: Error flag that tracks whether a validation problem has occurred during menu option processing. When set to 'Y', it signals that the menu screen should be redisplayed with an appropriate error message rather than transferring control to a sub-program.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-ON
variables.description: Condition name indicating that a menu processing error has been detected (e.g., invalid option, out-of-range selection, access denied). When true, the program suppresses navigation and redisplays the menu with an error message.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-OFF
variables.description: Condition name indicating that no error has been detected during menu option processing. When true, the program proceeds normally with the user's selected navigation action.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The CICS response code returned after executing CICS commands (such as reading the user security file or invoking a program). Used to detect whether a CICS operation succeeded or failed, enabling appropriate error handling during menu navigation.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The CICS reason code accompanying the response code, providing additional detail about why a CICS operation (such as a program availability inquiry for COPAUS0C) succeeded or failed. Used alongside WS-RESP-CD to determine the correct user-facing message or fallback behavior.

variables.name: WS-OPTION-X
variables.description: The raw alphanumeric representation of the menu option entered by the user on the screen, right-justified. Used as an intermediate holding field to receive the user's input before it is validated and converted to a numeric value for range and type checking.

variables.name: WS-OPTION
variables.description: The validated numeric menu option selected by the user (1 through the maximum available count). Drives the core business logic of the menu: determining which functional module (e.g., Account View, Credit Card List) to launch, and whether the selection is within range, admin-only, or a placeholder feature.

variables.name: WS-IDX
variables.description: A loop index counter used when iterating through the available menu options to build and display the menu on screen. Tracks the current position as the program cycles through each option entry (up to the maximum of 12 displayable options).

variables.name: WS-MENU-OPT-TXT
variables.description: A formatted display string combining the menu option number and its human-readable name (e.g., '1. Account View') for presentation on the menu screen. Constructed dynamically for each option during screen population so the user can see all available choices.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The standard CICS communication area passed between programs during screen navigation. Acts as the session handshake mechanism: its presence and content confirm that a valid authenticated session exists before the menu is displayed; if absent or empty, the user is redirected to the sign-on screen.

variables.name: LK-COMMAREA
variables.description: A single-byte placeholder within the CICS communication area used to detect whether a communication area was passed to this program. If this area is empty or zero-length, it indicates the user has not gone through proper authentication and must be redirected to the sign-on screen before accessing the menu.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central orchestration routine of the regular user menu program. It validates the user's session, determines whether to display or process the menu, routes the user's key press to the appropriate business action, and ensures the session remains active upon return.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph processes the user's menu selection when they press Enter, validating the chosen option number, enforcing access control rules, and launching the appropriate functional module — or displaying a meaningful message if the option is unavailable, restricted, or not yet implemented.

paragraphs.name: RETURN-TO-SIGNON-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Terminates the current menu session and redirects the user back to the bank's sign-on screen, ensuring a clean exit from the main menu. This acts as the system's safe logout navigation path, returning control to the authentication entry point of the CardDemo application.

paragraphs.name: SEND-MENU-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Assembles and renders the complete main navigation menu screen for the authenticated regular user, combining header information, available menu options, and any pending error or informational messages before presenting the screen for user interaction.

paragraphs.name: RECEIVE-MENU-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures the menu selection submitted by the user from the main navigation screen, reading whatever option number the user entered before pressing Enter. It is the entry point for processing the user's navigation intent within the CardDemo menu system.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.description: Prepares the screen header with current date, time, and application identity information before displaying the main menu to the user. This ensures every menu screen shows accurate session context and branding.

paragraphs.name: BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph dynamically constructs and populates the numbered list of functional menu options visible to the authenticated user on the main navigation screen, formatting each available feature as a numbered entry (e.g., '1. View Account Details') and placing it into the correct position on the display, up to a maximum of 12 options.
